reason: Gentle collisions can help the inner-disk stone and metal particles stick together before gravity takes over.

choice.combine: A mixture of stone and metal

expectation: The rocky particles should form larger aggregates.

effect: Gentle collisions produced rocky pebbles, but simple sticking alone will not keep growing them reliably.
reaction: The bouncing and fragmentation limit makes the next growth stage more interesting.
reason: Gas drag can change how pebbles move through the disk, helping them gather.
expectation: The gas drag should alter the pebbles' orbits and help concentrate them.

effect: Gas drag produced drifting rocky pebbles, which can concentrate in structured disk regions.
reaction: The link between gas drag and pebble drift is useful to see.
reason: A pressure maximum is a plausible place for drifting pebbles to accumulate.

choice.with: A pressure maximum in the disk

expectation: The pebbles should gather into a denser concentration.

effect: The pressure maximum concentrated the drifting pebbles into a dense rocky swarm.
reaction: It is satisfying to see concentration bypass the sticking problem.
reason: The dense swarm should allow gravity to gather the rocky solids into planetesimals.

choice.combine: A dense swarm of rocky solids

expectation: Gravity should collapse the swarm into rocky planetesimals.

effect: Gravity collapsed the dense rocky swarm into planetesimals, completing the rocky goal.
reaction: The progression from drifting pebbles to bound bodies is satisfying.
reason: The icy dust may grow into pebbles through gentle collisions, as the rocky mixture did.

choice.combine: An outer-disk store of ice and dust

expectation: Gentle collisions should form icy aggregates or pebbles.

effect: Gentle collisions made icy pebbles, giving the icy material a similar starting point to the rocky route.
reaction: The parallel between the two routes is clear.
reason: Gas drag caused rocky pebbles to drift, so it is a plausible next step for icy pebbles too.
expectation: The icy pebbles should drift through the disk under gas drag.

effect: Gas drag concentrated the icy pebbles directly through collective feedback, rather than the rocky route’s pressure trap.
reaction: The different concentration mechanism is an interesting contrast.
reason: As with the rocky swarm, gravity should bind the concentrated icy solids.

choice.combine: An icy swarm concentrated by gas drag

expectation: The icy swarm should collapse into icy planetesimals.

effect: Gravity bound the icy swarm into planetesimals, completing the chapter; they are possible water carriers rather than the only source of terrestrial hydrogen.
reaction: The two routes ended satisfyingly while retaining different concentration mechanisms.

mostWorthwhile.text: Concentrating the icy pebbles through gas drag was most worthwhile: the streaming-instability explanation showed how collective feedback can help gravity take over, in contrast to the rocky pressure trap.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making icy pebbles repeated the earlier gentle-collision step, though the parallel made the two routes easy to follow.

surprise.text: I expected icy pebbles to drift as the rocky ones did, but gas drag concentrated them directly through collective feedback.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; the choices followed the stated growth problem and the results explained the mechanisms.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the rocky and icy planetesimals contribute to later worlds, especially water delivery.
